question: What was the labour force participation rate for males in India as reported in the 6th Annual Employment-Unemployment Survey conducted by the Labour Bureau?
solution:
The correct answer is __**76.4%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The labour force participation rate (LFPR) is defined as the percentage of people in the labour force (employed + unemployed) within the working-age population.
 
• According to the 6th Annual Employment-Unemployment Survey (2016) conducted by the Labour Bureau, the LFPR for males in India was reported to be **76.4%**.
 
• The survey highlighted distinct gender disparities in LFPR, with male participation being significantly higher than female participation.
 
• The LFPR for males has traditionally been higher due to cultural, economic, and social factors influencing workforce participation in India.
 
• The survey serves as a critical tool for analyzing employment trends and policy planning to improve labour market outcomes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR):**

 
 
• LFPR measures the proportion of the working-age population (15 years and above) that is actively engaged in the labour market, either employed or seeking employment.
 
• It is a vital indicator of the economy's active workforce and economic activity levels.
 
 
 
• **6th Annual Employment-Unemployment Survey:**
 
 
• Conducted by the Labour Bureau, the survey provides insights into employment, unemployment, and labour force trends in India.
 
• The survey includes metrics such as LFPR, Worker Population Ratio (WPR), and Unemployment Rate (UR).
 
 
 
• **Gender Disparities in LFPR:**
 
 
• India has one of the lowest female LFPRs globally, attributed to factors like socio-cultural norms, lack of opportunities, and safety concerns.
 
• Efforts such as skill development and women-centric employment policies aim to improve female labour participation.
 
 
 
• **Policy Implications:**
 
 
• Data from employment surveys inform policymakers to address unemployment and improve workforce engagement.
 
• Programs like Skill India and Make in India aim to enhance job opportunities and labour force participation.
